startup.name: Drafted
startup.one_liner: Design your home instantly with AI
startup.description:
Drafted is building multimodal generative models for residential architecture and spatial design.

The product allows users to design homes by combining sketches and direct spatial input to generate coherent floor plans and elevations that can be explored in both 2D and 3D. Users can define footprints, lot boundaries, room placement, relationships, room programs, and square footage constraints that persist across generations and iterative design exploration, then export CAD, PDF, and other files into the rest of the home design and construction process.

More info on the company:
⁃ In the past month, we've had 120k users come to the site, generating 325k+ floor plans through socials and word-of-mouth. 
⁃ A team of 9, made up of researchers from Stanford, Autodesk, Brown, Adobe, and Architects from WeWork, Atmos, and design families
⁃ Raised $17.5M from investors such as Buckley Ventures (Josh Buckley), YC (Aaron Epstein), Patrick Collison, Evan Moore, Convective Capital (Bill Clerico), Ben Silbermann, Jack Altman, Samsung, Starship Ventures, Charlie Songhurst, Ryan Tedder, Moses Moody, Alex Blania, and Kevin Mahaffey

yc_acceptance.basis: Assumed accepted in this test, so this is a note. Published rate is about 1 percent of over 10,000 applicants (references/yc_acceptance.md). This company stated 120k monthly visitors, 325k plans generated, a nine person technical team and $17.5M raised from named angels and funds, which lifts it far above the starting rate.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC could say no because consumer AI design tools often show viral traffic without paying users, and the website visits may be curiosity from social posts. Residential architecture is also slow to monetize, and the company already has large funding so does not need YC.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Design software for homes is slow to monetize, and the strongest incumbents in the space, Autodesk and Matterport style players, have either bought or built similar tools. A generative design tool that does not become the workflow of record is likely to be sold small or fade.

killers.risk: Viral free usage does not convert to payment
killers.evidence: 120k visitors and 325k generated plans came from social media and word of mouth, which suggests curiosity usage; no revenue is stated.
killers.mitigation: Introduce paid export and pro tiers and report conversion.

killers.risk: Autodesk and general models add floor plan generation
killers.evidence: Autodesk has generative design products and large models can produce layouts from sketches.
killers.mitigation: Win on constraints, CAD export and architect trust.

killers.risk: Floor plans are a one time use case
killers.evidence: A homeowner designs a house rarely, so retention and lifetime value are low.
killers.mitigation: Sell to builders, architects and developers who design repeatedly.

killers.evidence: Generated plans that break building codes or structural rules lose professionals' trust.
killers.mitigation: Embed codes and have licensed architects review outputs.

technical_complexity.rationale: Multimodal generative models that respect constraints and output CAD files are hard, and the team of research engineers from Stanford, Autodesk and Adobe is suited to it. Data and spatial validity are the barriers.

takeover_risk.rationale: Autodesk has distribution and could build comparable generation inside 12 months, and general models are improving quickly. Mitigated by the head start in users and data.

evidence.claim: Homebuyers and builders pay architects and design services for plans, a large spend that software could capture.
Existing AI floor plan tools such as Maket have users, showing demand.

brand.rationale: A real word with a clear tie to drawing plans, similar to other YC real word brands. It helps consumer pull, though the generic word can be hard to find in search.

narrative.headline: Unusually strong early traction and funding for a 2026 YC company; the risk is monetizing a one time consumer use.
narrative.general_summary: Drafted arrives with funding, a research team and visible usage, so each funding step starts well above a typical YC company. The weakness is that floor plan design is episodic and incumbents can add similar tools, so the later rounds depend on turning free usage into paid professional use. It is a forecast from the input file and the base rates only, with no knowledge of what happened after the batch started, and the numbers should be read with wide error bars because the cohorts for these categories are small.
